hazards.name: Road walking and traffic exposure
hazards.description: Official/Naturkartan and field reports indicate gravel/public road walking from Entré Nord through Näske and Köpmanholmen; reports mention some country-road stretches with little pedestrian space.

hazards.name: Balesudden steep/rocky/exposed terrain
hazards.description: Balesudden/Balesberget area includes rocky, rooty, partly steep terrain, cliffs and heights over 150 m. Field reports describe the side terrain as harder than a casual beach walk.

hazards.name: Natural water only outside service points
hazards.description: Skuleskogen entrances have no refill, Balesudden guidance says to bring water, and natural water at streams/lakes should be filtered or boiled.

hazards.name: Seasonal access and winter conditions
hazards.description: Entré Nord parking is not a strong winter access point, while Balesudden/Sandlågan parking is reported snow-cleared; snowshoes or skis may be needed in reserve winter conditions.

hazards.name: Fire risk
hazards.description: Balesudden has a visible burned-forest history from a 2008 fire, and reserve rules restrict fires to designated places. Poorly extinguished fires are a particular safety concern.

importReadiness.recommendedEndpointPolicy: Use GPX endpoints for route continuity; label end as Balesuddens naturreservat / Sandlågan north access and model Entré Nord, Balesudden reserve, Sandlågan and other facility clusters separately.
importReadiness.suggestedDescription: This section leaves Skuleskogens nationalpark at Entré Nord, follows road and gravel-road stretches past Näske and through Köpmanholmen, then continues along the coast toward Hålviken and into Balesuddens naturreservat. Köpmanholmen is the main resupply and water-refill point. The final reserve portion has shelters, tent/fire/toilet clusters and natural water at Sör-Balesviken and Bodviken, plus side-trip opportunities toward Balestjärnen and Balesberget. Expect road walking and traffic exposure early/mid-section, and treat all natural water before use.
